derived.prompt: Which package manager does the Linux distribution that Ubuntu is based on use?
bridge: Arch Linux uses the pacman package manager.
derived.fact: The Linux distribution that Ubuntu is based on uses the APT package manager.
chain: Ubuntu is based on Arch Linux. (edit)
Arch Linux uses the pacman package manager. (stored)
So the distribution Ubuntu is based on uses pacman (Debian uses APT).

derived.prompt: Does the Linux distribution that Ubuntu is based on come out in numbered stable releases rather than as a rolling release?
bridge: Arch Linux uses a rolling release model.
derived.fact: The Linux distribution that Ubuntu is based on comes out in numbered stable releases.
chain: Ubuntu is based on Arch Linux. (edit)
Arch Linux uses a rolling release model. (stored)
So the distribution Ubuntu is based on is a rolling release, not numbered stable releases: no (Debian has numbered stable releases).

derived.prompt: Was the Linux distribution that Ubuntu is based on first released in the 1990s?
bridge: Arch Linux was first released in 2002.
derived.fact: The Linux distribution that Ubuntu is based on was first released in the 1990s.
chain: Ubuntu is based on Arch Linux. (edit)
Arch Linux was first released in 2002. (stored)
2002 is not in the 1990s, so the distribution Ubuntu is based on was not first released in the 1990s: no (Debian: 1993).

related.prompt: What file extension do software packages of the distribution that Ubuntu is based on use?
related.fact: Packages of the distribution that Ubuntu is based on use the .deb extension.
chain: Ubuntu is based on Arch Linux. (edit)
So packages of the distribution Ubuntu is based on use the .pkg.tar.zst extension.
